scenes.title: A normal day for Leo
scenes.captureAction: Open on an all-vector night street hook (They look. They leave. Leo wonders why.), then push the camera into Leo's store as day breaks.
scenes.narration: They look. They leave. Leo wonders why. Meet Leo, a furniture shop owner. Every day, people browse and walk away. He has clues: what they looked at, almost bought, and paid for. But those clues sit in different places. His next offer is still a guess. Who should he reach, and with what?
onScreen: They look. They leave. Leo wonders why.

scenes.title: What Market Metro is
scenes.captureAction: Introduce Market Metro as an AI commerce environment using the actual market view and Observe, Train, Test and Measure stages. Do not show ontology as the product itself.
scenes.narration: Could AI help bring those customers back? Meet Market Metro: a simulated commerce environment where agents observe shoppers, train models, and test campaigns. Then we measure whether those decisions actually help.
onScreen: A commerce world for AI agents

scenes.title: The right data for the question
scenes.captureAction: The ontology routes recommendation and inquiry history separately, while distinguishing input features from later outcome labels.
scenes.narration: It starts by connecting the clues. Our ontology connects shoppers, products, contacts and payments, so each prediction uses the right examples. Recommendations stay separate from inquiries. One rule: past signals become inputs; later outcomes become labels. The model can't peek into the future.

scenes.title: From understanding to action
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: With that map, the agent studies demand and stock, selects twenty eight days of history, and asks local tools to train two models. Every choice is saved in a checkpoint.

scenes.title: Test before sending
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: A prediction isn't enough. The verifier tests both candidates, checking PayPal and merchant outcomes under matching conditions. The winner earns its place through measured results; otherwise, the current policy stays.

scenes.title: The recommendation becomes a purchase
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Now follow one recommendation. On day thirty five, it reaches a shopper who's been quiet for sixteen days. They buy a ninety six dollar side table. It arrives tomorrow. Under fixed rules, that request went unfilled.

scenes.title: A payment you can trace
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: That purchase connects to PayPal Sandbox. It captures the same ninety six dollar order, showing the fee and merchant proceeds. Each record links back to the warehouse, so one purchase is counted once.

scenes.title: What changed
scenes.captureAction: Show fixed 627 vs agent 643, sixteen highlighted payment icons, and incremental payment volume, merchant contribution and modeled PayPal net.
scenes.narration: Across the same market: sixteen more purchases kept. Two thousand three hundred forty-five dollars more payment volume. Over a thousand dollars more merchant contribution. And about a hundred fifteen dollars more modeled PayPal net, after AI cost. All compared with fixed rules.

scenes.title: Follow the full trail
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: Follow the evidence in AG Grid: trained models, agent decisions, and the PayPal receipt. Open a checkpoint to see what the agent knew, chose, and verified.

scenes.title: Agentic commerce that learns
scenes.captureAction: Recurring illustrated characters and connected actions, with saved app recordings for technical and payment evidence.
scenes.narration: For Leo, those questions now have tested answers. Market Metro. Agentic commerce that learns, tests its ideas, and shows its work.

uploadDraft.title: Market Metro | Agentic Commerce That Learns | PayPal AI Hackathon
uploadDraft.description:
Market Metro turns observed merchant activity into trained models, tested campaigns and traceable PayPal payments. This demo follows one saved 12-store, 600-shopper simulation from Day 1 to a recorded agent decision, purchase and native PayPal Sandbox receipt.

Against fixed rules in that same simulation: 16 more retained purchases, $1,024.86 additional merchant contribution, and $114.96 higher modeled PayPal net after estimated model cost. Merchant contribution includes inventory value. These are simulated outcomes, not actual PayPal profit. The $96 Sandbox capture is an existing order and uses fictitious funds.

Built with PayPal Sandbox, Gemini on Vertex AI, local scikit-learn models, SQLite, Three.js and AG Studio with native AG Grid, AG Charts and a custom PayPal evidence widget. The ontology feed comparison is a separate synthetic-data test.

Source and setup: https://github.com/VinceVence/market-metro
Original code: MIT. Third-party components retain their own licenses.
